Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for joining the question-and-answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Energy Corp's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Taylor Voss, Chief Financial Officer; and Morgan Lee, Chief Development Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Solara Energy Corp delivered a solid performance in the Q3, driven by strong execution and growing demand for our renewable energy solutions. We are making significant progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding our project pipeline, enhancing our technological capabilities, and strengthening our partnerships.

I'd like to highlight four key aspects of our performance this quarter:

First, our capacity factor performance across solar, wind, and storage was outstanding, with a fleet-wide blended rate of 34.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year, reflecting top-tier efficiency from technology upgrades and favorable conditions.

Second, we secured 1.8 GW of new PPAs, pushing our contracted backlog to 12.4 GW and lifting our average realized PPA price to $38 per MWh, up 6% from last year.

Third, we refined our capacity addition guidance upward to 4.8-5.2 GW for full-year 2024 and 8-9 GW for 2025, backed by a 62 GW global pipeline that's converting at robust rates.

Fourth, we maintained disciplined debt levels at $5.2 billion gross, with net debt at $4.78 billion and an effective cost of debt compressing to 4.15%, positioning us for efficient scaling.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Voss to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Voss:
Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in the Q3. Our revenue was $920 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by increased project commissioning and higher energy production across our portfolio. Our gross margin was 44%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $380 million, primarily due to increased investments in research and development and sales and marketing. Our net income was $185 million, or $1.02 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.45 billion in cash and cash equivalents, including $420 million in unrestricted cash after adjustments. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

To provide deeper context on the key aspects Jordan highlighted, let me start with our capacity factor performance by technology, which underpinned much of our output this quarter. In Q3 2024, our fleet-wide blended capacity factor came in at 34.2%, a solid 210 basis points better than the 32.1% in Q3 2023. This strong showing came from favorable weather, repowering efforts, and ramping high-efficiency assets across our over 15 GWac operating portfolio. Breaking it down technologically, with some regional insights and the initiatives driving sustainability.

For solar PV, which makes up 42% of our operating assets, we hit an average capacity factor of 27.8%, up 180 basis points year-over-year. This puts us in the top quartile against NREL benchmarks, where U.S. utility-scale fixed-tilt systems average 25-26%. Over 60% of our solar features single-axis trackers from Nextracker's TrueCapture tech, pushing our performance ratio to 85.2%, improved from 82.1% last year. New bifacial modules from LONGi and JinkoSolar, with over 80% bifaciality, shone in projects like the 500 MW Gemini Solar + Storage in Nevada, which clocked 29.4% in its latest quarter. Regionally, U.S. Southwest assets in CAISO and ERCOT benefited from 5% above-P90 irradiance for 28.5% capacity factor. In Australia’s NEM areas like NSW, dust and La Niña effects limited us to 25.1%, but automated cleaning cut soiling to under 2%. Europe’s Spanish sites reached 26.8% with REPowerEU support. Our $150 million Solar Optimization Program retrofitted 1.2 GW with AI-driven MPPT from Enphase and GreenLancer analytics, dropping curtailment 15% to 1.8%. We're guiding FY24 solar at 28.5-29.5%, with perovskite tandems in pilots set to add another 300 basis points over two years, adding $220 million in EBITDA from merchant gains in ERCOT.

Moving to wind, our 8 GW portfolio—70% onshore, 30% offshore—achieved a blended 41.3% capacity factor, well above the IRENA onshore global average of 35%. Onshore delivered 37.9%, up 250 basis points, while offshore reached 49.8%, up 450. Onshore leaders in U.S. Midwest MISO and SPP used Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines with tall towers for 38.5%, on 8.2 m/s winds versus P50 7.9 m/s. Europe’s German onshore held 36.2% despite TSO congestion, aided by 20% intraday PPA. Offshore in the UK North Sea with Siemens Gamesa SG 14-222 DD turbines hit a record 51.2%, thanks to wake steering cutting array losses 12%. Our U.S. East Coast pre-commissioning models 52-55%. Repowering 800 MW onshore with larger 170m rotors and tall towers boosted turbine CF from 34% to 39%. WindSense AI from SCADA and Doppler LiDAR improved AEP forecasts 8%, reducing UK imbalance costs. Availability stayed at 98.7% with ice-throw fixes and LM Wind Power blade repairs. U.S. Great Plains winds were 7% above norm, though Iberia dipped 3%. We're putting 30% of 2024 capex into hybrids like the 400 MW Beacon Wind-Solar in Texas for 40%+ blended CF and IRA 45X premiums.

For energy storage, our 3.2 GWh fleet—20% of EBITDA—saw 62.4% utilization factor, up 450 basis points year-over-year, with 93.1% round-trip efficiency matching Tesla Megapack standards. In CAISO, 1 GWh arbitraged peaks at $250/MWh spreads for 68% utilization via frequency regulation and resource adequacy. ERCOT’s 850 MW/3,400 MWh Cascade rode storms for 71%, discharging 2.5 GWh weekly. Australia’s Hornsdale expansion with Neoen hit 58% but VPP with Sonnen reached 94.5% RTE. UK ESO contracts gave 60% via Fluence Mosaic multi-market stacking. Degradation is just 1.2% after 2,000 cycles using CATL LFP and thermal management. 500 MW hybrid solar+storage lifts plant CF 5 points. StorageAI Optimizer ML for 15-minute lookaheads captures 92% clip-and-ship, cutting aging 10%. With 2 GW/8 GWh queuing—including Form Energy iron-air 10-hour—we see 65-70% utilization as LCOS drops below $100/MWh for 15%+ ancillary returns.

These gains showcase our tech-led O&M, data forecasting, and geographic complementarity—U.S. assets at 98% wind-solar hedge. Risks like permitting and TOPCon shortages are countered by $2.5 billion IRA 45Y/48E tax transfers. FY24 blended CF guides to 35.0-36.5%, fueling 12-14% revenue growth and outpacing peers in merchant while PPAs de-risk at $35-45/MWh.

Next, on new PPAs secured and average pricing, another commercial highlight. In Q3, we locked 1.8 GW of new PPAs, growing our backlog to 12.4 GW—up 22% year-over-year, our best quarter since Q1 2022. This implies $4.2 billion lifetime revenue at 28% solar and 38% wind P50 capacity factors, with 2.5% CPI escalators in 85% hedging O&M inflation up 4-6%.

Breakdown: 1.2 GW U.S. Southwest solar in CAISO/ERCOT—850 MW fixed-price 20-year take-or-pay with PG&E and SCE, 350 MW VPPA with a Fortune 100 hyperscaler like our Google/Microsoft deals for 24/7 carbon-free. 500 MW SPP/MISO onshore wind hybrids with MidAmerican and data centers, using 4-hour LFP batteries against curtailment. 100 MW Australia NEM bifacial solar with Origin Energy, tapping Capacity Investment Scheme.

Fleet-wide average PPA price realized $38/MWh, up 6% from $36/MWh Q3 2023. Solar at $37/MWh (+9%), wind $40/MWh (+3%), blended $38/MWh excluding 5% merchant. Solar up from 15% module costs on LONGi Hi-MO 7 and 20% tracker yield; ERCOT strongest at $42/MWh. Wind gained $2/MWh IRA PTC inflation, hybrids +10-15%. Resilience from higher discount rates, PJM queue delays (2,500 GW pending), Big Tech RE100 (Amazon/Meta 10+ GW YTD per LevelTen). U.S. premiums: CAISO $41/MWh (LCFS), ERCOT $42/MWh, SPP $32/MWh. Australia $55/MWh AUD (LGC stacking), Europe €40/MWh despite German negatives.

Our edge: AI yield optimization with Enphase microinverters and First Solar Series 7 for 5-7% P90 uplift. Hybrids now 40% new PPAs, solving duck curve, ahead of NextEra/Orsted on softer volumes. FY24 adds 2.5-3 GW at $39-41/MWh, 30% storage-enhanced, funding 15-20% FFO CAGR to 2027. 70/30 contracted-merchant mix buffers IRA phaseout and tariffs.

Turning to capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets, as we commissioned 1.2 GW solar/storage in Q3 for YTD 2.1 GW, our outlook is strong on IRA momentum, REPowerEU auctions, and corporate PPAs. FY24 now 4.8-5.2 GW net adds, up from 4.5-5.0 GW: 3.5 GW bifacial TOPCon solar (1.4x DC:AC), 1.2 GW 4-hour BESS via SolaraStack. 70% H2 in ERCOT/PJM, queue attrition +15% YTD. 2025: 8-9 GW (65-80% ramp)—5.5 GW solar, 1.5 GW onshore wind (Vestas EnVentus-like), 1 GW U.S. offshore pilots, 1-1.5 GW storage. CAPEX $0.85-0.95/W solar-storage, 45X IRA on 80% U.S., EBITDA 25-28% at $35-45/MWh PPAs +200-250 bp financial hedges.

Three-year LTIP: 25-30 GW cumulative, to 40 GW operated by 2028 matching NextEra/Ørsted. Green H2 pilots to 500 MW by 2027 with Plug Power, fuel cell storage entry.

Pipeline at 62 GW, +18% QoQ/+45% YoY, $2.1B deposits/LOIs on 85% advanced. Origination 35 GW: India 8 GW SECI solar, LATAM 5 GW Chile/Brazil (>2,500 kWh/m²/yr Atacama). Early/mid 18 GW: 12 GW U.S. queues (2.5-year avg post-FERC 2023). Late-stage 9 GW: fully permitted, 95% PPA, 2 GW Texas BESS hybrids 90%+ RTE evening peaks. 25-30% five-year conversion, LTIP 18-22 GW probability-adjusted (vs. 28% historic).

Regions: U.S. 55% (15 GW ERCOT/SPP, 1 GW Microsoft-like PPA, 2 GW H2 PTC); Europe 25% (15 GW offshore 3 GW German/Dutch, 1 GW French hybrid like TotalEnergies Dunkirk); APAC/Emerging 20% (12 GW Australia REZ/India $0.22/Wp TOPCon, 1 GW UAE green ammonia).

Priorities: >12% IRR, <$25/MWh LCOE via Texas 2 GW/year module fab (First Solar, 30% domestic IRA). M&A like 4 GW 0.8x NAV carve-out. AI optimizers +8-10% bifacial, 300 MWh iron-air pilots. Risks: 100 bps rates shave 1-2% IRR, tariffs, elections—mitigated by 70% fixed SOFR+125 bps, $1.5B revolvers.

Finally, on debt levels and financing costs, core to scaling our 12 GW pipeline in solar PV, onshore wind, utility BESS. Tailored for asset-heavy renewables: project finance, green bonds, sustainability-linked to optimize WACC in volatile rates.

As of September 30, total gross debt $5.2B, +8% YoY from $4.8B, on $750M non-recourse for 1.2 GW Southwest Solar Hub, 500 MW Horizon Wind Texas. Net debt $4.78B after $420M unrestricted cash from PPA prepays/merchant tails. Leverage 3.4x net debt/LTM Adjusted EBITDA, in 3.0-4.0x target, below 4.2x peer avg (NextEra, Ørsted).

Composition: 55% U.S., 30% Europe, 15% LATAM/APAC. U.S. 70% non-recourse SOFR+165 bps (5.8% all-in hedged), 80% swaps to 2028 vs. Fed hikes. Europe North Sea 2 GW EURIBOR+210 bps (4.9%), €400M Q2 green bonds 3.75% fixed (20 bps greenium vs. legacy).

Effective cost 4.15%, down 65 bps from 4.8% YoY despite 5.3% IG rates. Drivers: Refinanced $300M 5.25% 2020 notes at 102% premium with $350M JPM/BNP sustainability RCF SOFR+140 bps tied to ESG/45% emissions cut by 2027. Green bonds: $600M 10-year August 4.1% (tightest post-Brookfield 3.9%), BlackRock/CalPERS demand for Article 9, refinanced Gemini 800 MW BESS CAISO RA/arbitrage. Hybrids: $200M tax equity GE Vernova/Invenergy monetizes 85% ITC at 7.5% IRR, cuts equity 25%. APAC Vietnam 400 MW floating solar JICA JPY TIBOR+90 bps.

Interest expense +12% QoQ to $52M (18% Adj EBITDA), but 22% op cash flow vs. 28% Q3'23 (15% FCF yield). FY interest $210M, Q4 $150M amortizations on 1 GW SunPath (98% contracted DC CF).

For lower rates post-Fed, target <4% WACC 2026: 60% fixed, $1B ATM shelf. Supports $3.5B capex (70% debt), BBB-/Baa3 ratings. Risks: Europe volatility post-Ukraine, IRA election—92% fixed PPAs, 15-year tenor buffer. Aligned with $1.7T BNEF renewables forecast for superior returns.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Jordan for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Taylor. In closing, I am confident that Solara Energy Corp is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Chen with Greenlight Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of SolaraStack on your project economics?

Jordan Hale:
Good morning, Sarah. Absolutely, SolaraStack, our proprietary hybrid dispatch optimization software, is proving transformative for project returns. It's enabling 15-20% uplift in dispatch revenues for our solar-plus-storage and wind hybrids by dynamically stacking energy arbitrage, frequency regulation, and resource adequacy services. For instance, in our 1.2 GW additions this year, it's boosted EBITDA margins by 3-5 points through AI-driven 15-minute lookaheads and 90%+ roundtrip efficiency capture. This de-risks LCOE below $25/MWh while commanding PPA premiums of 10-15%, directly supporting our 12-14% unlevered IRRs. We're rolling it out across the 62 GW pipeline, particularly the 9 GW shovel-ready queue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Vanguard Renewables. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
What are your expectations for grid connection timelines for your upcoming projects?

Morgan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Our grid connection outlook has improved markedly thanks to FERC Order 2023 reforms and queue attrition, bringing average timelines for our U.S. 12 GW early/mid-stage pipeline to 2.5 years from cluster studies. For H2 2024's 70% of 4.8-5.2 GW adds in ERCOT and PJM, we're on track for energization within six months post-shovel-ready, with 15% position gains YTD. Late-stage 9 GW is fully interconnected or queued first-position. Europe faces bottlenecks but our 1 GW French hybrid uses dynamic curtailment for mitigation. Globally, 85% advanced projects secured by deposits/LOIs ensure 25-30% conversion. Risks like volatility are hedged by 48E elective pay and $1.5B revolvers.

Operator:
Instructions for the question-and-answer session. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Jordan Hale for any closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Solara Energy Corp. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
